scope: Domain 1 first 50 single-answer questions (heuristic domain mapping)
notes: 11 of 50 reviewed; 39 pending. Source answer keys preserved. Q89 has flawed option wording.

items.reasoning: PrivateLink consumer interface endpoint connects privately to the SaaS provider endpoint service, with security groups limiting clients. No inbound access to company resources is exposed.

wrongOptions.A: Correct; consumer-side interface endpoint and endpoint security group.
wrongOptions.B: VPN requires tunnel management and does not provide the narrowly scoped SaaS endpoint pattern.
wrongOptions.C: Peering creates broad routed network connectivity and requires coordination.
wrongOptions.D: Reverses provider and consumer roles and exposes a company-provided service.

items.memoryTip: SaaS private API + no inbound exposure = consumer PrivateLink endpoint.

items.reasoning: A shared transit gateway connects spoke VPCs to the central egress VPC; spoke default routes and transit gateway routing forward outbound traffic through the egress VPC NAT gateway.

wrongOptions.A: VPC peering does not support transitive routing to another VPC's internet gateway/NAT egress.
wrongOptions.B: Correct hub-and-spoke centralized egress using a shared transit gateway.
wrongOptions.C: A transit gateway per account is unnecessary; NAT gateways are not direct TGW attachments.
wrongOptions.D: PrivateLink publishes individual services, not general-purpose internet egress.

items.memoryTip: Hundreds of VPCs + centralized NAT = Transit Gateway hub.

items.reasoning: PrivateLink endpoint services expose a particular application privately to interface endpoints, without requiring nonoverlapping VPC CIDRs or broad VPC routing.

wrongOptions.A: Overlapping VPC CIDRs complicate or prevent peering; secondary CIDR and NAT increase overhead.
wrongOptions.B: VPN appliances and NAT per business unit require ongoing management.
wrongOptions.C: Correct; provider endpoint service and consumer interface endpoints work with overlapping CIDRs.
wrongOptions.D: API Gateway private integration alone does not establish consumer network access or a private API.

items.memoryTip: Overlapping CIDRs + share one application = PrivateLink.

items.reasoning: MFA context for AWS CLI requests requires MFA-authenticated temporary credentials from STS GetSessionToken; deny S3 operations when aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent is not true.

wrongOptions.A: S3 bucket policies cannot interactively prompt a CLI user for an MFA code.
wrongOptions.B: IAM groups do not have assume-role trust policies.
wrongOptions.C: Long-term access keys lack MFA session context and would be denied.
wrongOptions.D: Correct; STS temporary credentials with MFA supply MFA context for S3 calls.

items.memoryTip: CLI + enforce MFA = STS GetSessionToken then use session credentials.

items.reasoning: Cross-account access is granted by IAM roles in the target member accounts, with trust allowing the management-account IAM user to assume them and permissions limiting resource actions.

wrongOptions.A: A role created only in the management account cannot directly confer target member-account resource permissions.
wrongOptions.B: Reverses the role placement and does not create the requested management-account user pattern.
wrongOptions.C: IAM groups cannot contain users from other AWS accounts.
wrongOptions.D: Correct; IAM user in management, least-privilege assumable roles in both members.

items.memoryTip: Cross-account action = role in target account, trusted caller in source.

items.reasoning: Site-to-Site VPN on a transit gateway supports encrypted IPv6 traffic; VPNs terminating on virtual private gateways do not support IPv6 traffic.

wrongOptions.A: Correct; attach VPC to transit gateway and connect the existing customer gateway using Site-to-Site VPN.
wrongOptions.B: Client VPN is intended for remote clients, not customer gateway site-to-site connections.
wrongOptions.C: Virtual private gateway Site-to-Site VPN does not support IPv6 traffic.
wrongOptions.D: Client VPN is not the site-to-site customer gateway solution.

items.memoryTip: IPv6 over encrypted Site-to-Site VPN = Transit Gateway, not VGW.

items.reasoning: An IAM role in the company account trusted by the auditors' AWS account grants scoped read-only permissions. A unique external ID helps mitigate the confused deputy problem for third-party access.

wrongOptions.A: External IDs are part of role assumption trust conditions, not generic resource policy configuration.
wrongOptions.B: Correct cross-account read-only role with external ID.
wrongOptions.C: Sharing long-term access keys violates recommended security practice.
wrongOptions.D: Creating local IAM users for external auditors increases credential management and is less secure.

items.memoryTip: External auditors + one AWS account = cross-account role + external ID.

items.reasoning: An API Gateway private REST API is accessed from a VPC through an execute-api interface endpoint. Endpoint policy and API resource policy restrict invocation to authorized endpoint and API.

wrongOptions.A: Site-to-Site VPN cannot be established to API Gateway as described, and API keys alone are not network isolation.
wrongOptions.B: Correct; private REST API with interface VPC endpoint and restrictive resource policy.
wrongOptions.C: API Gateway is not moved into a customer VPC, and transit gateway is unnecessary.
wrongOptions.D: Global Accelerator does not make the API private; API keys are not a private networking control.

items.memoryTip: Private API Gateway REST API = execute-api interface endpoint + resource policy.

items.reasoning: AWS Service Quotas quota request templates in the Organizations management account automatically request configured increases for newly created member accounts. This is less operational work than custom event-driven automation. Approval is not guaranteed.

wrongOptions.A: EventBridge/SNS/Lambda can request increases, but adds code and maintenance.
wrongOptions.B: Correct. Native Service Quotas organization quota request template.
wrongOptions.C: AWS Config evaluates configurations; it cannot directly set EC2 quotas.
wrongOptions.D: A custom Lambda creating Support cases is unnecessary and adds operational overhead.

items.memoryTip: New AWS account + repeat quota increases + least overhead = Service Quotas request template.

items.reasoning: An account created through AWS Organizations receives OrganizationAccountAccessRole by default. An authorized management-account principal assumes that role to administer the new member account, including creating IAM users.

wrongOptions.A: AWS Organizations does not email a 64-character root password.
wrongOptions.B: Correct. Assume OrganizationAccountAccessRole in the new account.
wrongOptions.C: The management account root password cannot authenticate the member account root user.
wrongOptions.D: An IAM user from the management account cannot directly sign into the new account using its own credentials; it must assume an authorized role.

items.memoryTip: Organizations-created account → OrganizationAccountAccessRole → assume role → create users.

items.reasoning: B captures the intended organization-wide resource perimeter using an RCP and aws:PrincipalOrgID, but it incorrectly says the RCP 'allows' access. Customer-managed RCPs use Deny statements; a valid implementation denies access for principals outside the organization, with service-principal exceptions as required. Treat B as the intended exam option, not a valid literal policy instruction.

wrongOptions.A: aws:PrincipalType=Service does not establish organization membership and the SCP approach does not protect against external resource principals.
wrongOptions.B: Intended answer, but wording must say deny outsiders, not allow insiders.
wrongOptions.C: aws:PrincipalAccount is a 12-digit account ID, not an organization ID; manual updates are high overhead.
wrongOptions.D: RAM account allowlists do not provide this organization-wide ECR resource perimeter.

items.memoryTip: RCP = resource perimeter; aws:PrincipalOrgID = organization identity; enforce with explicit Deny.
